fences.rule: If the item names where a stream of deals comes from, including a referral a past counterparty makes, it is there; if it names why flow bends toward a node at a price the seller would not otherwise accept, and what a second node does to it, it is here.
fences.case: The contractor named by other contractors at the moment they decline the job, an unpaid funnel the refusers run.

fences.rule: If the item is a point where a small input moves a large output, the scarce input at the narrow hour or the register's smallest edit, it is there; if it is what the position does to what arrives unbidden, it is here.
fences.case: The tow truck that answers at three in the morning, when the searcher's horizon collapses to whoever picks up.

fences.rule: If the item is the move of acquiring the bottleneck, it is there; if it is what holding the adjoining position does to which lots are brought first, it is here.
fences.case: Acquiring the physical bottleneck through which all traffic must flow, as an act taken to foreclose rivals.

fences.rule: If the toll is still paid at a gate with a free bypass nobody remembers, the power is obsolete and it is there; if the onboarding the open file saves is a real cost the counterparty would otherwise pay, it is here.
fences.case: The incumbent bank that gets the next loan because the borrower is already onboarded and the file is open.

fences.rule: If the name or reputation is what the seller wants for itself as consideration, it is a category of value there; if the name is wanted because third parties cannot close without it, it is here.
fences.case: The anchor tenant whose signature the other tenants' leases are conditioned on.

fences.rule: If the question is what the volume of arrivals does to the node's criteria, it is there; if it is what bends the arrivals toward the node in the first place, it is here.
fences.case: A fund whose bar drifts as each deck is judged against the recent stream rather than the underlying bar.
